chapterName: Early Rome & the Kingdom: The Foundation of an Empire (753-509 BCE)

questions.question: Why did the classicist Mary Beard call Romulus "Mr Rome"?
options: He was the only king born inside the city
He personally designed every Roman temple
Roman coins always showed his portrait
He was Rome's first elected consul
His name was probably invented from the city's name
questions.explanation: The name Romulus was probably made up from the name of Rome itself, hence "Mr Rome". Most modern historians treat the founding legend as myth.
questions.sourceQuote: Even the name Romulus was probably invented from the city's name, making him, as the classicist Mary Beard put it, "Mr Rome".

questions.question: What was the role of the augur in making a new king?
options: He sought signs that the gods approved
He crowned the king in the Forum
He presented the king to the Senate
questions.explanation: The augur, a priest, took the king-elect up to the citadel to look for signs of divine approval. Only after this did the assembly grant the king imperium.
questions.sourceQuote: A priest called an augur took the king-elect up to the citadel and looked for signs that the gods approved.

questions.question: After Romulus vanished in a storm, a respected nobleman claimed Romulus had appeared to him in a vision as which god?
questions.explanation: The nobleman said Romulus had appeared as the god Quirinus. Others whispered that the nobles had murdered the king and hidden the pieces of his body.
questions.sourceQuote: But one respected nobleman claimed Romulus had appeared to him in a vision as the god Quirinus.

questions.question: On which hill have archaeologists found traces of Bronze Age settlement, possibly from as early as 1700 BC?
questions.explanation: The earliest traces of settlement come from the Capitoline Hill, possibly as early as 1700 BC. Huts appeared on the Palatine much later, by the 9th or 8th century BC.
questions.sourceQuote: Archaeologists have found traces of Bronze Age settlement on the Capitoline Hill, possibly from as early as 1700 BC.

questions.question: Why do historians find the traditional 243 years for Rome's seven kings hard to believe?
options: Archaeology shows Rome had only three kings
It leaves no time for Romulus's founding
The dates contradict the Gallic sack
It means an average reign of almost 35 years
No king is mentioned by any Greek writer
questions.explanation: Seven kings across 243 years gives an average reign of almost 35 years, which seems far too long. This is one reason modern historians treat the traditional story cautiously.
questions.sourceQuote: Seven kings ruling for 243 years means an average reign of almost 35 years, which seems far too long.

questions.question: According to Livy, how did the warlike King Tullus Hostilius die?
options: He fell in battle against Alba Longa
He vanished in a storm while reviewing troops
Jupiter burned him and his house with lightning
He drowned while crossing the Tiber
He was murdered by a son of Ancus
questions.explanation: Tullus had scorned the gods. When he finally begged Jupiter for help as he lay dying, the god struck him with lightning after a 32-year reign.
questions.sourceQuote: According to Livy, when the dying king finally begged Jupiter for help, the god burned him and his house with lightning.

questions.question: Which king adopted the immigrant Tarquinius Priscus as a son?
questions.explanation: After settling in Rome, Tarquinius won the favour of King Ancus Marcius, who adopted him. He went on to become Rome's fifth king.
questions.sourceQuote: After settling in Rome he won the favour of King Ancus Marcius, who adopted him as a son.

questions.question: Which great building project did Tarquin the Proud complete?
options: The temple of Jupiter on the Capitoline
Rome's first bridge over the Tiber
The Temple of Diana on the Aventine
questions.explanation: Tarquin the Proud finished the great temple of Jupiter on the Capitoline Hill. He was an energetic ruler who made Rome the leading power among the Latin cities.
questions.sourceQuote: He finished the great temple of Jupiter on the Capitoline Hill.

questions.question: The authors of the American Federalist Papers took their pen name from which early Roman?
questions.explanation: The Federalist authors signed themselves "Publius" after Publius Valerius Poplicola, one of the leaders of the revolt. French revolutionaries likewise named boys and towns after Brutus.
questions.sourceQuote: French revolutionaries named boys and towns after Brutus, and the authors of the American Federalist Papers signed themselves "Publius" after Poplicola.

questions.question: Which natural advantages did the site of Rome offer early settlers? (select all that apply)
options: A deep natural harbour on the sea
Rich silver mines in the hills
A ford across the Tiber River
questions.explanation: A ford let travellers cross the Tiber, and steep, defensible hills rose from a fertile plain. These advantages existed long before Rome had any king.
questions.sourceQuote: A ford let travellers cross the Tiber River in central Italy, and a cluster of steep, easily defended hills rose from a wide, fertile plain.
